prompt: What is the value of 2019 tenths?
Each of the five shapes shown below is made from five unit cubes. Which has the smallest surface area?

solutions.title: Count joined faces
solutions.body:
Five separate cubes have total surface area $5\times6=30$. Each time two faces are joined, the surface area decreases by $2$. Shapes A to D each have four joins, giving area $22$, but shape E has five joins, so its area is $20$, the smallest.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: There are 120 000 red squirrels living in Scotland. This represents 75% of their total UK population. How many more red squirrels live in Scotland than live in the remainder of the UK?

solutions.title: Use fractions
solutions.body:
Scotland has $\frac34$ of the UK squirrels, so the rest of the UK has $\frac14$, which is one third of the Scottish number: $\frac13\times120\,000=40\,000$. The difference is $120\,000-40\,000=80\,000$.

**Answer: (D) 80 000**

prompt: A 24-hour digital clock shows the time in hours and minutes. How many times in one day will it display all four digits 2, 0, 1 and 9 in some order?

The answers to the three calculations below are to be written in descending order.

- $X$: $0.6\times0.5+0.4$
- $Y$: $0.6\times0.5\div0.4$
- $Z$: $0.6\times0.5\times0.4$

What is the correct order?

The diagram shows part of a tessellation of the plane by a quadrilateral. Khelen wants to colour each quadrilateral in the pattern so that no two quadrilaterals that meet (even at a point) have the same colour. What is the smallest number of colours he needs?

solutions.title: Lower and upper bound
solutions.body:
At certain points four quadrilaterals meet, and they all touch each other, so at least $4$ colours are needed. The official solution shows a colouring that uses exactly $4$ colours, so $4$ is the minimum.

**Answer: (B) 4**

prompt: How many positive cubes less than 5000 end in the digit 5?

solutions.title: Cubes of numbers ending in 5
solutions.body:
A cube ends in $5$ only if the number does. $5^3=125$ and $15^3=3375$ are less than $5000$, but $25^3>20^3=8000$. So there are $2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

prompt: Three consecutive positive integers less than 20 are, in ascending order, prime, even and triangular. What is the product of these three integers?

solutions.title: Triangular numbers
solutions.body:
The triangular numbers below $20$ are $1,3,6,10,15$. The last of the three integers follows an even number, so it is odd: $3$ or $15$. With $3$ the first would be $1$, not prime; with $15$ we get $13,14,15$ with $13$ prime. The product is $13\times14\times15=2730$.

**Answer: (E) 2730**

prompt: What is the value of $7-6\times(-5)-4\times(-3)\div(-2)$?

solutions.title: Order of operations
solutions.body:
$7+30-(4\times(-3)\div(-2))$. Now $4\times(-3)=-12$ and $-12\div(-2)=6$, so the expression is $7+30-6=31$.

**Answer: (C) 31**

prompt: A recent report about the amount of plastic created in the last 65 years stated that the 8.3 billion tonnes produced is as heavy as 25 000 Empire State Buildings in New York or a billion elephants. On that basis, how many elephants have the same total weight as the Empire State Building?

solutions.title: Divide
solutions.body:
25 000 buildings weigh as much as $10^9$ elephants, so one building weighs $\frac{10^9}{25\,000}=\frac{10^6}{25}=40\,000$ elephants.

**Answer: (B) 40 000**

prompt: Which of the following is equal to $\dfrac{3^9}{9^3}$?

The game of Rorrim$^2$ is played on a $4\times4$ board, starting with a counter in one corner, as shown. At each turn, the player moves the counter to a cell that is the reflection of its current cell in one of the six dashed lines. How many cells could the counter occupy after precisely three turns?

solutions.title: Colour the board like a chessboard
solutions.body:
Colour the board like a chessboard with the starting corner unshaded. Every reflection in a dashed line moves the counter to a cell of the opposite colour. So after three turns the counter is on a shaded cell: at most $8$ cells. Checking, each of the $8$ shaded cells can be reached in three reflections. So the answer is $8$.

**Answer: (C) 8**

prompt: Megan writes down a list of five numbers. The mean of her first three numbers is $-3$. The mean of her first four numbers is $4$. The mean of her first five numbers is $-5$. What is the difference between her fourth number and her fifth number?

solutions.title: Sums
solutions.body:
The first three numbers sum to $-9$, the first four to $16$, the first five to $-25$. So the fourth number is $16-(-9)=25$ and the fifth is $-25-16=-41$. Their difference is $25-(-41)=66$.

**Answer: (A) 66**

prompt: There are four people, some of whom always tell the truth. The others always lie. The first person said, "An odd number of us always tell the truth". The second person said, "An even number of us always tell the truth". The third person said, "A prime number of us always tell the truth". The fourth person said, "A square number of us always tell the truth". How many of these four people were telling the truth?

solutions.title: Reason about the statements
solutions.body:
A number cannot be both odd and even, so exactly one of persons 1 and 2 tells the truth. No number is both prime and square, so at most one of persons 3 and 4 tells the truth. Hence $1$ or $2$ people tell the truth. If exactly $1$ did, statements 1 and 4 would both be true (1 is odd and a square), a contradiction. If $2$ did, then persons 2 and 3 are the truth-tellers (2 is even and prime), which is consistent. So the answer is $2$.

**Answer: (C) 2**

prompt: The diagram shows six congruent equilateral triangles, of side-length 2, placed together to form a parallelogram. What is the length of $PR$?

solutions.title: Right triangle
solutions.body:
Drop a perpendicular from $R$ to the line $PQ$ extended (with $Q$ the next vertex), meeting it at $T$. Triangle $QTR$ has a $60^\circ$ angle at $Q$ and hypotenuse $QR=2$, so $RT=2\sin60^\circ=\sqrt3$ and $QT=2\cos60^\circ=1$. The base $PQ=6$, so $PT=7$. By Pythagoras, $PR^2=7^2+(\sqrt3)^2=52$, so $PR=2\sqrt{13}$.

**Answer: (A) $2\sqrt{13}$**

prompt: Two numbers $x$ and $y$ have a product which is equal to their sum. Which of these expressions gives $x$ in terms of $y$?

solutions.title: Rearrange
solutions.body:
$xy=x+y$ gives $xy-x=y$, so $x(y-1)=y$ and $x=\frac{y}{y-1}$. (Division by $y-1$ is fine: $y=1$ would give $x=x+1$, impossible.)

**Answer: (A) $\frac{y}{y-1}$**

prompt: Which of these is equal to $0.\dot8+0.0\dot7$?
Two numbers $x$ and $y$ are such that $x+y=\frac23$ and $\frac xy=\frac23$. What is the value of $x-y$?

solutions.title: Solve for y
solutions.body:
$\frac xy=\frac23$ gives $3x=2y$. Multiply $x+y=\frac23$ by $3$: $3x+3y=2$, so $2y+3y=2$ and $y=\frac25$. Then $x=\frac23-\frac25=\frac4{15}$ and $x-y=\frac4{15}-\frac6{15}=-\frac2{15}$.

**Answer: (B) $-\frac2{15}$**

prompt: Which of these expressions has the largest value?

solutions.title: Compare in a chain
solutions.body:
$\frac16+\frac17+\frac18+\frac19+\frac1{10}>\frac16+\frac17+\frac18+\frac1{10}+\frac1{10}=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18$ (D), since $\frac19>\frac1{10}$ and $\frac1{10}+\frac1{10}=\frac15$. Similarly D$>\frac15+\frac16+\frac18+\frac18=\frac14+\frac15+\frac16$ (C), and C$>\frac14+\frac16+\frac16=\frac13+\frac14$ (B), and B$>\frac14+\frac14=\frac12$ (A). So E is largest.

**Answer: (E)**

solutions.title: Decimals
solutions.body:
A$=0.5$, B$\approx0.583$, C$\approx0.617$, D$\approx0.634$, E$\approx0.646$. E is the largest.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: Three equilateral triangles with sides of length 1 are shown shaded in a larger equilateral triangle. The total shaded area is half the area of the larger triangle. What is the side-length of the larger equilateral triangle?

solutions.title: Area ratio
solutions.body:
The shaded area is half the large triangle's area, so the large triangle has area $6$ times that of a unit triangle. Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of the side lengths, so the large side is $\sqrt6$ times $1$.

**Answer: (B) $\sqrt6$**

prompt: The diagram shows a right-angled triangle $PQR$. The point $S$ is the midpoint of the side $QR$ and $\tan\angle QPR=\frac32$. What is the value of $\sin\angle QPS$?

solutions.title: Choose lengths
solutions.body:
The right angle is at $Q$. Let $PQ=4x$. Then $\tan\angle QPR=\frac{QR}{PQ}=\frac32$ gives $QR=6x$, so $QS=3x$. By Pythagoras, $PS=\sqrt{16x^2+9x^2}=5x$. So $\sin\angle QPS=\frac{QS}{PS}=\frac35$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac35$**

prompt: Four of the following six-digit integers are always divisible by 7, regardless of the values of the digits $P$ and $Q$. Which of the following is not necessarily a multiple of 7?

solutions.title: Look for factors of 1001 and 10101
solutions.body:
$1001=7\times143$, so any number of the form $XYZXYZ=1001\times XYZ$ is a multiple of $7$ (options A and D). Also $10101=7\times1443$, so $XYXYXY=10101\times XY$ is a multiple of $7$ (options B and C). But $PPPQQQ=111\times(1000P+Q)=3\times37\times(1000P+Q)$ need not be: e.g. $P=1,Q=2$ gives $1002=7\times143+1$.

**Answer: (E) $PPPQQQ$**

prompt: The diagram shows a triangle with sides $n^2+n$, $2n+12$ and $3n+3$. What is the sum of all the values of $n$ for which the triangle is isosceles?

solutions.title: Three cases
solutions.body:
Case 1: $n^2+n=2n+12\Rightarrow(n-4)(n+3)=0$. $n=-3$ gives a negative side, but $n=4$ gives sides $20,20,15$, valid. Case 2: $n^2+n=3n+3\Rightarrow(n-3)(n+1)=0$. $n=-1$ gives a side $0$, but $n=3$ gives $12,18,12$, valid. Case 3: $2n+12=3n+3\Rightarrow n=9$, sides $90,30,30$, which fails the triangle inequality. So the valid values are $3$ and $4$, with sum $7$.

**Answer: (A) 7**

prompt: When 5655 is divided by a two-digit positive integer $N$, the remainder is 11. When 5879 is divided by the same positive integer $N$, the remainder is 14. What is the sum of the digits of $N$?

solutions.title: Subtract
solutions.body:
Write $5655=Nj+11$ and $5879=Nk+14$. Subtracting, $224=N(k-j)+3$, so $N(k-j)=221=13\times17$. So $N\in\{1,13,17,221\}$. A remainder of $14$ requires $N>14$, so $N=17$ (221 has three digits). Digit sum $1+7=8$.

**Answer: (C) 8**

prompt: The diagram shows three touching semicircles with radius 1 inside an equilateral triangle, which each semicircle also touches. The diameter of each semicircle lies along a side of the triangle. What is the length of each side of the equilateral triangle?

solutions.title: Right triangles at the vertices
solutions.body:
Let the triangle be $PQR$ and let $S$ and $T$ be the centres of the semicircles on sides $PQ$ and $QR$. The semicircles touch, so the line of centres passes through the touching point and $ST=1+1=2$. The semicircle centred at $T$ touches side $PQ$ at $W$, with $TW=1$ perpendicular to $PQ$. In right triangle $SWT$, $\sin\angle WST=\frac12$, so $\angle WST=30^\circ$. In triangle $SQT$, $\angle Q=60^\circ$ and $\angle QST=30^\circ$, so $\angle STQ=90^\circ$. Hence $SQ=\frac{ST}{\sin60^\circ}=\frac4{\sqrt3}$. Also the semicircle centred at $S$ touches side $PR$ at a point at distance $1$ from $S$, and $\angle P=60^\circ$, so $PS=\frac1{\sin60^\circ}=\frac2{\sqrt3}$. Therefore $PQ=PS+SQ=\frac6{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: (D) $2\sqrt3$**
